description: The Democratic Republic of Congo has imposed a hard cobalt export quota — a 96,600 t/yr ceiling for 2026-27 (~48% of 2024 output) — with unused H1 quota forfeited to the ARECOMS reserve after the 2026-06-30 deadline. Cobalt has repriced ~+160% off its Feb-2025 lows to ~$26/lb (~$57,320/t cobalt hydroxide CIF China) on the sovereign supply squeeze. Nickel is the softer counterpart: structural surplus, range-bound ~$17-18.8k/t, with Indonesia not yet finalizing its 2026 RKAB quota (target ~260-270 Mt vs 379 Mt in 2025, ~one-third compression) — a second, milder supply lever. Directly relevant to cobalt_nickel: a discrete, sovereign, timestamped supply shock (textbook EventCatalyst, decays on quota relaxation) that stacks on top of the struct_battery_storage_supercycle demand structural. Caveat: LFP-battery substitution away from cobalt caps the durable upside, so the sector-level catalyst is asymmetric — a sharp near-term price lever, not a permanent re-rating.
